title: Mirabai
summary: Mirabai was a sixteenth-century Rajput princess and Hindu mystic poet-saint who became one of the central figures of the North Indian Bhakti movement. Devoted entirely to the deity Krishna, whom she regarded as her divine spouse, she defied the strict aristocratic conventions of the royal Rajput household into which she married. Her ecstatic devotional lyrics, or bhajans, survived through oral and manuscript traditions and remain widely celebrated across South Asia.

uncertainty.note: Traditional dates place her birth around 1498 and death around 1546–1547.

as_recorded.value: born, around 1498, a princess in the Mewar region of present-day Rajasthan, India

where.modern_name: Chittorgarh, Rajasthan, India (site of Chittor Fort, where she lived as a Mewar princess and composed devotional poetry)

importance.justification: Eminent Bhakti mystic poet-saint whose devotional lyrics to Krishna transformed medieval vernacular literature in northern India.
